jurisdiction.name: Portugal
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Portugal steers AI through Council of Ministers acts: the National Digital Strategy (2024) and the National AI Agenda, approved in January 2026 with a governance model and 32 initiatives for 2026-2030, replacing the earlier AI Portugal 2030 strategy (2019) in practice. A 2026 decree-law requires prior authorisation for public-sector AI projects, the 2021 Charter of Human Rights in the Digital Age has an article on AI and algorithmic decisions, and the state technology agency (ARTE) publishes the GuIA guide for AI in public services. The law implementing the EU AI Act, with the communications regulator ANACOM as lead authority, is still pending; the data protection commission (CNPD) issued a 2026 opinion on AI in public procurement.
lead_institutions: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
Agency for Technological Reform of the State (ARTE)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The law implementing the EU AI Act and ANACOM's designation are still pending and are listed as leads.

instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Agenda (ANIA): AI at the service of society and Portugal's competitiveness
instruments.current_status: Standalone agenda document dated January 2026 (author: Governo de Portugal) on digital.gov.pt (page updated 08.01.2026); formally approved as annex I of Council of Ministers Resolution 2/2026 (i-0bd1f56f2511).
instruments.summary: Portugal's national AI agenda, framed as Action #20 of the 2026-27 Action Plan of the National Digital Strategy. It sets six guiding principles (including responsible innovation and the State as catalyst) and four pillars (infrastructure and data; innovation and adoption; talent and skills; responsibility and ethics), operationalised through 32 initiatives across universities, research centres, companies and public administration. It is aligned with the EU AI Continent Action Plan and Apply AI strategy.

instruments.english_title: GuIA: Guide to Artificial Intelligence (ethical, transparent and responsible AI)
instruments.issuing_authority: Agency for Technological Reform of the State (ARTE), originally Agency for Administrative Modernisation (AMA)
instruments.current_status: Current version v.1.3 dated March 2026 (ARTE); digital.gov.pt page (author AMA) last updated 30.06.2025. Earlier AMA versions were not dated on the page.
instruments.summary: Public-administration guide (84 pages, version 1.3) promoting progressive adoption of ethical, transparent and responsible AI, produced under the 'Responsible AI' project. It is organised in three parts: values, principles and recommendations; assessment dimensions; and an ethical risk-assessment tool, with an executive summary published separately. It refers to the EU trustworthy-AI requirements (ALTAI) and covers risks such as deepfakes.

instruments.english_title: Decree-Law No. 85/2026 creating the State Simplification and Technology Network
instruments.current_status: Published in Diário da República, 1st series, No. 71, 13 April 2026 (approved by Council of Ministers 26 February 2026, promulgated 2 April 2026). The text read contains no specific entry-into-force article, so effective_date is left null.
instruments.summary: Decree-law creating the State Simplification and Technology Network under the minister for State reform, with a Coordination Committee for the Digital Strategy, and abolishing the Council for Digital in Public Administration (revoking RCM 94/2024). Article 6(1)(c) requires direct and indirect State administration bodies, including public enterprises, to obtain the Committee's prior authorisation for artificial intelligence projects developed by or for them, alongside large IT procurements, sovereign cloud and data-centre projects.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rule subjecting public-sector AI projects to central prior authorisation.

instruments.english_title: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 2/2026 approving the National Artificial Intelligence Agenda and its governance model
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of Ministers (Presidency of the Council of Ministers)
instruments.current_status: Published in Diário da República, 1st series, No. 5, 8 January 2026 (approved 4 December 2025); in force the day after publication (para. 6). The official digital.gov.pt page links the Diário da República PDF. Monitoring body (Council for Digital in Public Administration) was abolished by Decree-Law 85/2026, whose Coordination Committee for the Digital Strategy now follows strategic documents.
instruments.summary: Resolution approving the National Artificial Intelligence Agenda (ANIA, annex I) and its Action Plan (PAANIA) for 2026-2030 (annex II). The plan has 32 initiatives in four pillars (infrastructure and data; innovation and adoption; talent and skills; responsibility and ethics), including defining the national AI Act competent authorities, coordination model and sanctions regime (IV.4), AI regulatory sandboxes (IV.5) and a national AI Act implementation guide with risk-assessment tools (IV.6). The plan is updated by the member of Government for State reform with finance, and monitoring was assigned to the Council for Digital in Public Administration.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Formal government act adopting Portugal's current national AI strategy and action plan.

instruments.official_title: Lei n.º 27/2021 — Carta Portuguesa de Direitos Humanos na Era Digital
instruments.english_title: Law No. 27/2021: Portuguese Charter of Human Rights in the Digital Age
instruments.current_status: Published in Diário da República, 1st series, No. 95, 17 May 2021; enters into force 60 days after publication (art. 23), i.e. 16 July 2021. Later amendments to other articles were not reviewed; art. 9 checked in the original text.
instruments.summary: Law approving the Portuguese Charter of Human Rights in the Digital Age. Article 9 requires the use of AI to respect fundamental rights, balancing explainability, safety, transparency and accountability and avoiding bias and discrimination; decisions with significant impact taken by means of algorithms must be communicated to those concerned and be open to appeal and auditable; robots are subject to beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy and justice principles.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with an explicit AI and algorithmic-decision provision (art. 9).

instruments.english_title: AI Portugal 2030: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence

instruments.current_status: Published in English in 2019 (DGES news item of 3 June 2019 says it was launched 'this year' by INCoDe.2030 and links this PDF). The 2026 National AI Agenda is now the main national AI instrument; no official act formally revoking AI Portugal 2030 was found. The incode2030.gov.pt site returned HTTP 503 / connection reset.
instruments.summary: Portugal's first national AI strategy, launched in 2019 under the INCoDe.2030 digital skills initiative and presented by the Minister of Science, Technology and Higher Education. It sets objectives of economic growth, scientific excellence and human development, with action lines including AI in public administration and its modernisation, and a chapter on ethics and safety.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI strategy; predecessor of the 2026 National AI Agenda.

instruments.current_status: Published in Diário da República, 1st series, No. 151, 8 August 2019; in force the day after publication (art. 68(1)). Later amendments not reviewed.
instruments.summary: Portugal's GDPR implementing law. It sets the organisation and powers of the CNPD as the national supervisory authority and adds national rules on specific processing, including video surveillance and employees' biometric data, which frame the processing of personal data by AI systems in Portugal.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National data protection law governing personal-data processing for AI training and use; CNPD's statute.

instruments.summary: Resolution approving Portugal's National Digital Strategy (EDN) and its governance model. The strategy identifies AI as one of the century's major opportunities and aims to maximise safe, ethical and responsible adoption of AI across health, agriculture, education and business; its structuring initiative No. 10 is the National AI Agenda, later approved by RCM 2/2026.

instruments.official_title: Parecer/2026/39 — Projeto de Decreto-Lei que altera o Código dos Contratos Públicos
instruments.english_title: CNPD Opinion 2026/39 on the draft Decree-Law amending the Public Contracts Code (including use of AI in public procurement)
instruments.current_status: Approved at the CNPD meeting of 2 June 2026. Non-binding opinion on a draft; the resulting decree-law was not identified (see leads).
instruments.summary: Opinion requested by the Secretary of State of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers on a draft decree-law to simplify and digitalise public procurement, including the use of digital and artificial intelligence systems in procurement procedures. The CNPD recommends documentation, auditability, explainability and bias testing of algorithmic systems, limits on reuse of data for algorithmic training, mechanisms for explanation, contestation and human oversight, and training of procurement staff, and questions whether a decree-law is the right instrument.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection authority's position on AI use in public procurement.
